headline: FIDELITY TO GO OVERWEIGHT GOLD AGAIN — Ian Samson Targets 2027 Bull Return; Plans 5% Allocation in $3B Income Fund
snippet: Fidelity International multi-asset portfolio manager Ian Samson told Kitco News the firm plans to rebuild its gold position — targeting approximately 5% of their $3 billion income and growth strategy fund — after neutralizing their position following gold's January peak near $5,589, calling the $4,000 level a compelling entry point ahead of what he expects to be a renewed bull run by 2027. Samson said the bullish thesis remains intact as long as central banks continue accumulating and governments resist orthodox fiscal restraint.

headline: ALLIED CRITICAL METALS HITS TUNGSTEN — 23.8m at 0.68% WO3, Peak 2.96%; 6 Rigs Active at Borralha, Portugal (CSE:ACM)
snippet: Allied Critical Metals (CSE: ACM) released the first assay results from its 2026 campaign at Borralha, Portugal, with inaugural hole Bo_13/26 returning 23.8 metres at 0.68% WO₃ including 4.0 metres at 2.96% WO₃ — and a broader envelope of 57.6 metres at 0.30% WO₃ — confirming the Santa Helena Breccia as a bulk-tonnage tungsten system underpinning the project's recently completed Preliminary Economic Assessment. Six rigs are drilling with a seventh arriving shortly for the 20,000-metre campaign.

headline: AMERICAN EAGLE NAK: 280m at 0.96% CuEq From Surface, 154m at 1.21%; South Zone Extends 100m North in BC Babine District (TSXV:AE)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / American Eagle Gold Corp.
snippet: American Eagle Gold (TSXV: AE) kicked off its 2026 season at the NAK copper-gold porphyry in British Columbia's Babine district with hole NAK26-83 returning 280 metres at 0.96% copper equivalent from surface, including a high-grade core of 154 metres at 1.21% CuEq that extends the South Zone 100 metres north — the first of approximately 80 holes planned for NAK's largest-ever 50,000-metre campaign. The result positions NAK alongside B.C.'s most active bulk-tonnage porphyry programs this year.

headline: AZTEC TOMBSTONE DOUBLES DEPTH — 155.4m at 1.63 g/t AuEq; Arizona Oxide Zone Expands 300m West and South (CVE:AZT)
snippet: Aztec Minerals (CVE: AZT) drilled hole TR26-30 at its Tombstone project in southeast Arizona, returning 155.4 metres at 1.08 g/t gold and 30.23 g/t silver (1.63 g/t AuEq) from the Contention target — doubling the known mineralised depth and expanding the oxide gold-silver footprint approximately 300 metres west and south. Results are drawn from 84 reverse-circulation holes plus the program's first core assay, and the company notes that step-out drilling is still confirming the southern and depth extents.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD PERMITS MUD LAKE — 93 g/t Au Surface Sample; Drilling August to Extend High-Grade Shear Zone in Ontario (TSXV:DRY)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Dryden Gold Corp.
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSXV: DRY) secured the exploration permit to drill its Mud Lake target at the Gold Rock camp in Ontario's Dryden gold district, where a high-grade shear zone similar to the flagship Elora system returned surface samples of 93.00 g/t gold — suggesting the Manitou Dinorwic deformation zone could host multiple gold deposits along strike. Drilling is planned for early August and will test periodicity at the deposit scale north of the previously permitted area.

headline: SILVER AT $58.55, 52% BELOW ATH — FOMC July 28 Is the Binary; June CPI Drop to 3.5% Shifts Odds; LBMA Targets $79.57
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 silver price outlook identifies the July 28-29 FOMC meeting as the single most important near-term catalyst for a metal sitting at $58.55 — 52% below its January all-time high of $121.62 — noting that June CPI's surprise decline to 3.5% from May's 4.2% has pushed rate-hike odds below 10% and reduced real-yield headwinds. Institutional consensus points sharply above spot: LBMA analyst consensus sits at $79.57/oz, JPMorgan's base case is $81/oz, while the structural sixth-consecutive supply deficit and growing solar demand remain intact.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTHS UP IN JULY — Dysprosium +25.4% to $261/kg; NdPr Alloy Hits New 2026 High at $133/kg
source_name: Rare Earth Mining / Rare Earth Market Outlook
snippet: Every one of the 18 rare earth elements tracked in July 2026 posted price gains, led by dysprosium's 25.4% surge to $261.63/kg — its largest single-month move of the year — and NdPr alloy's 21.4% rise to $133.02/kg, clearing the March peak and setting a new 2026 high as a second consecutive annual supply deficit presses against EV motor and wind turbine demand. Germanium gained 27.8% domestically while indium jumped 26.5%, reflecting tightening critical minerals supply chains that have persisted despite modest China export quota adjustments.

headline: FIVE BANKS WEIGH IN ON GOLD'S Q2 SELLOFF — Institutions Diverge on Whether $4,000 Holds Into the FOMC Meeting
snippet: GoldSilver.com aggregates responses from five major financial institutions to gold's Q2 selloff from the $5,589 January peak to below $4,000, finding a genuine divide: some argue $4,000 represents a structural floor supported by central bank accumulation and miner margins near $3,000/oz, while others warn that Middle East-linked oil-driven inflation could extend the Fed hiking cycle and push real yields higher before the July 28-29 FOMC decision. The piece maps the $3,830–$4,260 range as the tactical battlefield, with institutional flows likely determining the direction of the next $400 move.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: MINING STOCKS AT GENERATIONAL OPPORTUNITY — Equities Lag Bullion Like Never Before; Record FCF Season Begins
snippet: Brien Lundin argues in his GoldSeek editorial that gold and silver mining equities are presenting one of the rarest entry setups in two decades: stocks that have significantly outpaced the S&P 500 year-to-date while simultaneously trading at historically deep discounts to the gold price itself, a divergence that has historically resolved sharply when institutional attention turns to the sector. With Q2 2026 earnings season beginning and producers expected to report record free cash flow on roughly $4,500/oz average realised gold, Lundin identifies the current pullback as the most compelling accumulation window he has seen since the last major sector re-rating.

headline: GOLD MAJORS DELIVERING NEAR-RECORD Q2 — $4,500 Average Price Drives Blowout Margins; Kinross Next on July 29
snippet: Gold mining producers are reporting strong Q2 2026 results driven by an average realised gold price near $4,500/oz — Equinox Gold delivered 176,836 ounces, Aura Minerals posted 75,437 gold equivalent ounces — with producer cash costs averaging well below $1,500/oz implying margins above $3,000/oz, among the widest in sector history. Kinross reports July 29 and Barrick follows shortly after, with the broader Q2 earnings parade expected to test whether record cash flows finally close the persistent valuation gap between bullion and mining equities.
